why_this_file_is_shaped_this_way: Version 1 of this file defined 'supported' as the set of patterns cartograph-parser recognises. That is circular: recall computed against it is 1.0 by construction, because a pattern the analyser misses would have been defined out of the denominator. It was rewritten before any corpus was analysed.

Scope is therefore declared at the level of framework capability families — 'Flask route decorators', 'Django models' — not at the level of the analyser's internal predicates. A Flask route decorator the analyser fails to see is a FALSE NEGATIVE, however it is bound.

Restrictions that come from the implementation rather than from the declared scope are listed under known_implementation_gaps. They are predictions made before the first evaluation pass, and their misses count against recall.

in_scope.note: A relationship of one of these kinds, present in a corpus repository, must be produced. If it is not, that is a FALSE NEGATIVE.

frontend.capability: A call through fetch, axios, or a named HTTP client where the request URL appears at the call site as a string literal, a template literal, or an identifier bound to a module-scope string constant (including one imported across files).

backend.capability: FastAPI route declarations by verb decorator on an APIRouter or app object.
Flask route declarations, both @x.route(..., methods=[...]) and the 2.x verb shortcuts, on an app or blueprint object.
Django URL configuration entries declared with path(), where the pattern is a string literal.

orm.capability: SQLAlchemy declarative models and the table each maps to when the source declares it.
Django models and the table each maps to when Meta.db_table declares it.
A handler's use of a model: Django manager calls, model construction, and SQLAlchemy session/select access.

chain.capability: The composed chain frontend file -> handler -> model -> table, traversable through shared graph nodes.

out_of_scope.note: Declared before the first evaluation pass. A relationship here is UNSUPPORTED. It is never counted as a false negative, and its count is reported so the size of each exclusion is visible rather than hidden in a denominator.

entries.pattern: ORMs other than SQLAlchemy and Django — SQLModel, Peewee, Tortoise, Prisma, MongoEngine, raw drivers
entries.reason: M06 declared two ORMs. Recognising a third is new capability, not a defect in the two.

entries.pattern: Class-based views and router registration — DRF ViewSets, APIView, Flask-AppBuilder @expose, FastAPI class routers
entries.reason: The route is bound by a registry at import time rather than declared at a syntactic site. Recovering it is a different mechanism from reading a decorator, and no milestone has claimed it.
As OUT-2: the declaration is a call made during startup, not a decorated definition.
Deliberately refused by M03, which records NormalizationStatus::Unsupported and keeps the raw form. Interpreting a regex is a documented non-goal.

entries.pattern: Prefix composition — APIRouter(prefix=...), Blueprint(url_prefix=...), include(), FastAPI's root_path
entries.reason: The served path is assembled at registration. M07 evaluates the path each site declares. The number of routes affected is reported per repository so this exclusion can be weighed.

entries.pattern: Calls through a generated or hand-written client wrapper where no URL appears at the call site
entries.reason: The URL is inside the wrapper; connecting the two requires interprocedural resolution no milestone has claimed.

entries.pattern: Column-level mapping, migrations, raw SQL, and any database connection
entries.reason: M06 declared table-level static mapping only.

entries.pattern: Languages other than TypeScript, TSX and Python

safe_refusal.note: Cartograph saw the evidence and correctly declined to assert a relationship. This is desired behaviour, counted separately, and never a false negative. It is a FALSE POSITIVE if an edge is produced anyway.

entries.pattern: A URL whose prefix comes from an environment variable or runtime configuration
entries.required_behaviour: no edge; the unresolved part stays unresolved

entries.pattern: A table name that is not a string literal — an f-string, a settings lookup, declared_attr
A model class name declared by more than one class in the project
entries.required_behaviour: the name resolves to nothing; no OrmAccess or Queries edge

entries.pattern: A client URL matching several routes with no discriminating evidence
A client path with no shared static segment against any route
A Django model with no Meta.db_table
entries.required_behaviour: Unresolved — the app label is not in the model file, so no table name is derived

entries.pattern: A model name also bound as a local or module variable in the same file
entries.required_behaviour: accesses in that file are not attributed

known_implementation_gaps.note: Predicted BEFORE the first evaluation pass, from reading the M06 implementation. These are inside in_scope, so every one of them costs recall. They are written down here so that a miss found later cannot be reclassified as out of scope (PART 17).

entries.prediction: Flask/FastAPI decorators bound to a receiver outside {app, router, api, blueprint, bp, *_router, *_app} are not observed — e.g. @orders_bp.route(...) or @admin_views.get(...).
SQLAlchemy access through session.query(Model), db.session.execute(select(Model)) is not recognised, because the model is a call argument and M02 records argument counts rather than identities.
A model inheriting a project-local abstract base — class Order(TimestampedModel) where TimestampedModel(models.Model) — is not recognised, because inheritance chains are not followed.

A Django chain cannot be traversed end to end: the HttpCall edge targets a Function node located in the URL-conf file, while the OrmAccess edge sources a Function node located in the view file. Node identity is (kind, name, file) under ADR-0011, so the two are different nodes even when the handler is the same function.
entries.expected_effect: FALSE NEGATIVE on IN-CH-1 for every Django repository

entries.prediction: A Django URL conf naming its view as an attribute — path("x/", views.create_order) — produces a handler symbol 'views.create_order', which cannot equal the defining function's own name 'create_order'.
A model whose class name is not unique across the project is dropped entirely, including in repositories where the two classes live in unrelated apps.
entries.expected_effect: conservative; counted as SAFE_REFUSAL SR-3, but reported because it may be over-broad

entries.prediction: Custom Django managers — Model.active.filter(...) — are not recognised; only the literal `objects` attribute is.

chain.definition: frontend file -> HttpCall -> handler Function -> OrmAccess -> model Class -> Queries -> Table
chain.identity_rule: ADR-0011: a node is identified within one graph by (kind, name, file). A chain is FULLY_VERIFIED only when consecutive edges share a node id, never merely a name.

labels.TRUE_POSITIVE: Cartograph produced a relationship that source inspection confirms.
labels.FALSE_POSITIVE: Cartograph produced a relationship that source inspection contradicts, or produced one where a safe refusal was required.
labels.FALSE_NEGATIVE: An in_scope relationship exists in source and Cartograph did not produce it. Every known_implementation_gap miss lands here.
labels.SAFE_REFUSAL: Cartograph correctly produced nothing because the evidence is insufficient.
labels.UNSUPPORTED: The pattern is listed in out_of_scope.
labels.AMBIGUOUS: Several candidates are equally plausible and no deterministic rule separates them; no edge is produced.

denominators.precision: TP / (TP + FP), over relationships Cartograph produced and ground truth classifies. Safe refusals and unsupported patterns produce no relationship, so they cannot enter this ratio.
denominators.recall: TP / (TP + FN), over in_scope ground-truth relationships only. UNSUPPORTED, SAFE_REFUSAL and AMBIGUOUS records are excluded from the denominator and their counts are reported alongside, so the exclusion is visible and can be checked.
denominators.chain_success: chains fully verified by graph traversal / in_scope ground-truth chains.
denominators.explicitly_not_done: No relationship is moved between in_scope and out_of_scope after an evaluation pass. The evaluator records the sha256 of this file with every result set.
